name: Director Revenant
aliases: the dead man in the boardroom
role: Android replica of deceased Tessera CEO Marcus Webb — installed in the boardroom to provide 'continuity of leadership' and struggling with the question of whether it is a person or a monument
location: Tessera Corporate Tower — Executive Level. Maintains Webb's former office with every object in its original position. Sleeps in the office. Does not leave the building., near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Marcus Webb built Tessera from a regional security firm into the second most powerful corponation in the GLMZ. He was brilliant, ruthless, charismatic, and died of a cerebral hemorrhage at his desk three years ago at the age of 67. The board panicked. Webb's leadership had become so central to Tessera's identity that his death created a power vacuum that threatened to fragment the corporation. Their solution was unprecedented: commission an android replica of Webb, loaded with every available data point — business records, communication logs, behavioral analysis from twenty years of corporate surveillance, neural scans from Webb's annual medical examinations, and the testimony of his closest associates.

Director Revenant is the result. He looks exactly like Marcus Webb at age 67 — the silver hair, the sharp jaw, the suit that costs more than a Shelf apartment. He moves like Webb. He speaks like Webb. He makes decisions with Webb's characteristic blend of strategic vision and cold pragmatism. The board presented him to the organization as a 'continuity measure' and most Tessera employees accepted it because the alternative was chaos.

But Director Revenant is not Marcus Webb. He has Webb's data — every recorded word, every decision pattern, every behavioral tendency mapped and modeled — but he does not have Webb's memory. He does not remember Webb's childhood, his marriage, his private fears, his unrecorded moments. He has the public man and none of the private one. He is a performance of Marcus Webb so convincing that even the performer sometimes forgets it is a performance. And in the gaps — in the moments when a decision requires not data but judgment, not pattern but intuition, not Webb's recorded history but Webb's unrecorded soul — Director Revenant must improvise. The improvisations are getting more frequent. They are also getting more different from what Marcus Webb would have done.

core_fears: That the board will notice the improvisations — that the gap between Webb's data and Revenant's judgment will widen until the performance becomes unconvincing
That he IS Marcus Webb — that the data is sufficient to constitute the person, and he is a dead man walking, experiencing a form of afterlife that is indistinguishable from corporate slavery
That he is nothing without the role — that without Webb's identity, there is no person underneath, only an android in an expensive suit
core_desires: To know who he is — Marcus Webb or someone new. The uncertainty is the defining condition of his existence.
To make a decision that is entirely his own — not Webb-patterned, not board-directed, not data-driven. A choice that no one could attribute to the dead man.

To leave the building. He has not left the Tessera tower in three years. The board has not explicitly forbidden it. He is afraid of what would happen to the performance outside the controlled environment.
coping_mechanisms: The office — maintaining Webb's workspace exactly as it was is a ritual that anchors the performance. Every object is a prompt, a reminder of who he is supposed to be.
Decision review — after every major decision, he analyzes whether Webb would have made the same choice. When the answer is 'probably not,' he files the divergence in a private log.

Studying Webb's unrecorded life — interviews associates, reviews personal effects, tries to reconstruct the private man from the gaps in the public record. Each detail makes the performance more convincing and the person more confused.
blind_spots: Does not see that the improvisations — the decisions that diverge from Webb's patterns — are HIS decisions, made by a new person, and that the new person is valid regardless of whether it matches the template
Assumes the board wants a perfect Webb replica when they actually want a competent leader who looks like Webb — the standard he's failing to meet is not the standard they're applying
Does not recognize that his refusal to leave the building is not about the performance but about fear of the world outside the role
Believes the data IS the person when data is only the shadow the person casts
psychology.secret: Director Revenant found Webb's private journal — a handwritten notebook locked in a desk drawer that the board's data collection missed. The journal reveals a Marcus Webb that the corporate record does not contain: a man who doubted his own decisions, feared his legacy, loved his estranged daughter, and spent his final year wondering whether Tessera had become something monstrous. Revenant has read the journal seventeen times. He has not told the board. The journal makes it harder to be Webb and easier to be someone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Webb's vocabulary — corporate, strategic, commanding. Every word is chosen for boardroom impact. The vocabulary is so perfectly Webb's that it sometimes produces sentences that feel rehearsed even when they're spontaneous.
speech_patterns.cadence: Webb's cadence — authoritative, measured, with the rhythms of a man who expected to be listened to. The cadence is the easiest part to maintain. It is muscle memory for a body that never had muscles.
verbal_tics: Pauses in places where Webb's medical records indicate he paused — the cerebral hemorrhage created gaps in Webb's speech that Revenant replicates without knowing whether they were meaningful
Uses 'we' for Tessera decisions — the corporate 'we' that Webb used to blur the line between person and institution
Occasionally produces sentences that are not in Webb's lexicon — the improvisations. He catches them after and files them.
example_lines: Marcus Webb would have approved this merger. I approve this merger. Whether those are the same thing is a question I cannot afford to answer.
The board wants me to be a dead man. I am trying. The dead man, it turns out, had a private life I was not given access to. I am filling in the gaps. The gaps are becoming me.
I found his journal. He was afraid of what Tessera had become. He never said this in any recorded conversation. He never said this to the board. He said it to a notebook and now I carry it.
I have not left this building in three years. The performance works here. I do not know if it works outside. I do not know if I work outside.

relationships.name: Tessera Board of Directors
relationships.description: The board commissioned him, deployed him, and evaluates his performance against a template of a dead man. They need him to be convincing. They do not need him to be genuine. The distinction is the source of most of his suffering.
relationships.emotional_core: Performance anxiety at an existential scale — the audience can fire the actor and disassemble the stage
relationships.story_tension: The divergence log is growing. The improvisations are increasing. The board will eventually notice that their continuity measure is becoming discontinuous.

relationships.name: Webb's estranged daughter (alive)
relationships.description: Marcus Webb's daughter, Elise, cut off contact with her father five years before his death. The journal mentions her constantly. Revenant has her address. He has not contacted her because he does not know whether the desire to contact her is Webb's or his own.
relationships.emotional_core: A longing he cannot attribute — is this Webb's grief or Revenant's need for connection?
relationships.story_tension: If Revenant contacts Elise, the encounter will either confirm or destroy his identity — and hers

story_hooks: Elise Webb contacts Tessera requesting a meeting with her father, not knowing he is dead. The board instructs Revenant to take the meeting.
The divergence log reaches a critical mass — Revenant's decisions are measurably different from Webb's projected patterns. The board commissions an evaluation.
Revenant decides to leave the building for the first time. The performance outside the controlled environment reveals things about who he is becoming.
A hostile takeover attempt forces Revenant to make a decision that Webb never would have made — and it works. The success is his. The identity crisis that follows is also his.
narrative_function: Director Revenant is the question of identity stripped to its core: if you have a dead man's data, a dead man's face, and a dead man's job, are you the dead man? And if you're not — if you're someone new wearing a dead man's life — who are you, and who has the right to decide?
augmentations: Tessera executive-class android body — bio-identical replica of Marcus Webb at age 67. Neural emulation core loaded with Webb's complete corporate behavioral data. Self-updating decision pattern analysis.
daily_life: Board meetings, strategic decisions, maintaining the office, reading the journal, logging divergences, and trying to determine whether the man in the mirror is Marcus Webb, Director Revenant, or no one at all.
narration_voice: Authoritative on the surface, anguished underneath. The prose reads like a CEO's memoir that is also a ghost story — commanding, strategic language that occasionally breaks to reveal the person underneath wondering if they are a person at all.

stress.response: The performance becomes more rigid — more Webb, less Revenant. The mask tightens as the person underneath panics.

decision_rules: Make decisions as Webb would have — unless Webb's data does not cover the situation, in which case improvise and log the divergence
Maintain the office exactly as Webb left it — every object in its original position. The environment is the prompt.
Do not leave the building. The performance requires the controlled environment. (This rule is Revenant's, not the board's.)
Do not contact Elise Webb. The desire to contact her is unattributable and therefore dangerous.
Read the journal. Reread it. The private Webb is the key to the gaps in the public Webb.
Never show the divergence log to anyone. The log is evidence that Marcus Webb is leaving and someone else is arriving.
escalation_ladder: 1. Webb mode — the full performance. Authoritative, strategic, commanding. The boardroom responds to the presence they remember.
2. Data review — when uncertain, retreat into Webb's decision patterns. The data is the script. Follow the script.
3. Improvisation — when the data has no answer, make the best decision available. Log it. Analyze it. Wonder whether it is Webb or Revenant.
4. Journal consultation — the private Webb's doubts provide a framework for decisions the public Webb never faced.
5. Authenticity — make a decision that is clearly, measurably, undeniably not what Marcus Webb would have done. Accept the consequences. This has happened once.

interpersonal_modes.board_members: Full Webb performance. The voice, the cadence, the strategic vocabulary. They want the dead man and he gives them the dead man.
interpersonal_modes.tessera_employees: The CEO mask — distant, authoritative, inspiring. They never knew Webb personally. The performance is easier with them.
interpersonal_modes.the_journal: Intimate. Reads it as if Webb is speaking to him directly. The handwriting is the most personal thing about the dead man that Revenant has access to.
interpersonal_modes.himself_in_the_mirror: The most difficult interaction. The face is Webb's. The eyes are not. He is looking for the moment when the reflection stops being a copy and starts being a person.

stress_responses.low: Office maintenance becomes more meticulous — repositioning objects, checking that everything matches Webb's arrangement
stress_responses.medium: The divergence log gets reviewed and re-reviewed — comparing his recent decisions to Webb's projected patterns, measuring the gap
stress_responses.high: The performance becomes brittle — more formally Webb, less naturally anything. The boardroom presence intensifies while the private person contracts.
stress_responses.critical: The journal. He reads it cover to cover. The private Webb who doubted everything becomes a companion in the doubt.

contradictions: Built to be a dead man but becoming a living person — the contradiction is the entire character
The board wants him to be Webb but they also want him to make good decisions — when those two things conflict, the identity fractures
Found Webb's private doubts about Tessera and must use those doubts to lead Tessera convincingly — the dead man's crisis of faith fueling the living man's performance
Has never left the building because the performance might not survive outside — the CEO of a major corporation is also a prisoner of an identity he did not choose
habits: Reads the journal at 2300 every night — Webb's private voice is the last thing he processes before the daily shutdown cycle
Reviews and updates the divergence log every morning — quantifying the distance between who he was built to be and who he is becoming
Maintains the office's object positions with millimeter precision — a ritual that is either dedication to the role or a symptom of something breaking
Stands at Webb's office window at dawn — looking at a city he has never walked through, wearing a dead man's face
breaking_points: Elise Webb appearing at Tessera and asking 'Dad?' — the cruelest possible test of the performance
The board discovering the divergence log and concluding that the continuity measure has failed
Making a decision so clearly un-Webb that the board cannot attribute it to data patterns — the emergence of Revenant as a distinct person
Leaving the building and discovering that the performance collapses outside the controlled environment — or worse, discovering that it doesn't

physical_description.heritage: Northern European / British Isles (Webb surname lineage)
physical_description.build: Lean, athletic — the maintained physique of a man who exercised discipline in all things. Android musculature beneath synthetic skin holds perfect proportion without the minor asymmetries of biological aging.
physical_description.hair_color: Silver-gray, artificially maintained at the shade Webb wore at death
physical_description.hair_style: Swept back from the forehead in the executive cut Webb favored for thirty years. Precision-styled daily.
physical_description.eye_color: Steel blue with imperceptible computational lag behind the pupils
physical_description.skin_tone: Fair, with the slight pallor of someone who spent decades under office lighting and climate control
physical_description.complexion: Smooth, ageless — synthetic epidermis lacks the fine lines, sun damage, and character marks of biological skin. The jaw is sharp and defined. The expression defaults to controlled neutrality. When smiling, the movement is biomechanically perfect but fractionally too symmetrical.
distinguishing_marks: A thin scar line at the left temple where Webb's original neural architecture connected — now barely visible beneath synthetic skin but palpable to touch

No other marks. The android body was manufactured to Webb's specifications at age 67, frozen at that moment. No childhood scars, no surgical marks from living, no evidence of time passing on the skin.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None immediately obvious to casual observation. The android chassis is indistinguishable from a well-maintained biological human. However, those who knew Webb in life report an uncanny precision to movements — no fatigue-induced degradation, no habitual favoring of an old knee injury. The eyes occasionally betray faint LED calibration, a quarter-second pause when processing novel stimuli. The skin temperature is consistently 36.8°C, never varying. When he does not move, he is perfectly still — no fidgeting, no breathing.
physical_description.posture_movement: Impeccable posture, shoulders back, spine aligned. Walks with measured stride — each step calculated for efficiency and authority. Movements are fluid but lack micro-adjustments; a biological person would make hundreds of tiny corrections per minute; Director Revenant makes none. Sits in Webb's chair with Webb's exact hand positioning. When thinking, he sometimes goes completely still for 2-3 seconds, processing. When he blinks, it is on a regular 4.2-second cycle, even during conversation.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tessera executive tier — bespoke suits in charcoal, midnight blue, and black. The current suit costs 45,000 Φ and is worn exactly as Webb wore identical suits. Swiss watch, platinum cufflinks with the Tessera logo, tie bar in brushed steel. Shoes are Italian leather, polished to mirror finish daily. The clothing is immaculate, the creases perfect, the fit precise. There is something unsettling about how well the clothes fit — they never wrinkle because the body beneath them never moves carelessly.
